newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks up from slump on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks up from slump on foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks, unfazed by the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, closed up for the first time in 10 days on foreign buying of a blue chip, brokers said.

The all share index, which closed up for the first time since February 6, ended 2.61 points higher at 617.57. Highly capitalised blue chip John Keells Holdings rose 10.50 rupees to 190.50 and Tokyo Cement 2.50 to 60.

"With the index stuck at a stage where it will not move at market levels, the buyer would have had to pay up to get the quantity of John Keells Holdings," said Prasanna Chandrasekera, a trader at brokerage John Keells.

The share began rising on news Sri Lanka had signed a deal with South Asia Gateway Terminals, a joint venture between Peninsular and Oriental steam Navigation Co (PO.L) and John Keells, for a $1 billion Colombo port facilities expansion.
Turnover was 62.21 million rupees on 653,835 shares on foreign buying of JKH and local buying of Hayleys. Foreign buying was 42.8 million rupees and selling was 21.5 million.
"The movement on John Keells shows that a serious buyer will have to pay up to collect quantity," said Thikshan Arulampalam, a trader at Lanka Securities. -- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
